name: website
title: Website
description: The pages of a finished website crawl. Each page is read for the products and needs it holds; a page that holds none is set aside.

files.config.yaml:
# WHAT A PERSON SETS TO RUN THIS PIPELINE: the Import form, rendered by the canvas the way a
# node's config is. Only what the collect steps do not know by themselves.
configSchema:
  type: object
  required: [runId]
  properties:
    runId:
      type: string
      title: Crawl run
      description: >-
        The finished Apify run to read, its run id from the Apify console. Every page the
        run produced lands in the inbox.
      default: ""
      placeholder: abc123XYZ
"ui:order": [runId]
files.interface.yaml:
# A PIPELINE ON A CANVAS, as a node: its URLs may come from an upstream node instead of the
# form, and its rows go downstream. The collect steps' nodes carry their own credentials, so
# this declares none.
inputs:
  - name: signal
    type: object
    description: URLs to start from, when wired from an upstream node instead of the form
    required: false

outputs:
  - name: rows
    type: array
    description: The inbox rows this run collected, held until they are run
  - name: total
    type: number
    description: How many rows this run collected

credentials: []
files.pipeline.yaml:
unoverse: "1.0"
# A PIPELINE IS THE SOURCE SIDE: how content is collected and which objects it may yield.
# It never knows how an object is built; that is the object's own api/service.yaml. Between
# collect and the map sit the platform's steps, the same for every pipeline and every
# object: known, understand, make detail, match, retire, save (docs/unoverse/data/pipelines/README.md).
# A pipeline fills the collect slot and names its yields. It adds no step of its own.
type: pipeline
name: website

# THE FACE, as a node's node.yaml carries it.
title: Website
description: >-
  The pages of a finished website crawl. Each page is read for the products and needs it
  holds; a page that holds none is set aside.
whenToUse: >-
  Bring a crawled site onto the map. The crawl has already run; give this the run to read.
  Every page lands in the inbox, held, until you run it.
category: Pipelines
version: 1.0.0
color: "#00B4A6"
logoUrl: https://res.cloudinary.com/sonik/image/upload/v1751511484/gravity/icons/apifyLogo.png

# COLLECT: the nodes that fetch, in order. Each step names a marketplace node and fills its
# config; a later step would read an earlier step's outputs by name (`{{ collect.pages.total }}`).
# The nodes carry their own credentials, hosts and interface; nothing is repeated here. The
# org's Apify key is found by type, or picked in the form when the org holds more than one.
# The crawl itself is not this pipeline's to start (owner, 2026-09-09: "we can assume that's
# done; it will collect the output of a run"): one step, the run's pages.
collect:
  - name: pages
    node: ApifyResults
    config:
      runId: "{{ config.runId }}"

# THE ROW each collected item becomes: the inbox's fields from the item's, and nothing else
# the crawl returns (its html, screenshot, debug, keywords, JSON-LD die here). `sourceId` is
# what the platform's known step hashes against; the crawl already derives it from the
# content, so an unchanged page is known before any model call. The text is the page's
# markdown when the crawl saved it, the whole page, so the first sweep sees what the page
# says (owner ruling 2026-09-09: the crawl's 300-character summary found one need where the
# page held five); a crawl run with text only gives its text. The image is the page's own
# Open Graph choice, a list, so one `return` expression.

# WHAT THIS PIPELINE MAKES (docs/unoverse/data/pipelines/README.md layer 1, ruled 2026-09-10): every page is
# read for its needs, and a page MAY be a product, which the model says on the thin look and
# the product then reads whole. Two entries over the same page merge into one inbox item,
# so a page is still one model call. Only the source knows what identifies its content, so
# the address and content are said here.
make:
  # EACH PAGE, READ ONCE: the needs it speaks to, and maybe a product; the model says.
  - each: "{{ collect.pages.items }}"
    sourceUrl: "{{ item.url }}"
    sourceId: "{{ item.contentId }}"
    content:
      title: "{{ item.metadata.title }}"
      description: "{{ item.metadata.description }}"
      image: "return ((item.metadata.openGraph || []).find(g => g.property === 'og:image') || {}).content"
      text: "return item.markdown || item.text"
    need: { cardinality: many }
    product: { cardinality: one, any: true }
files.test.yaml:
# THE PIPELINE UNDER GUARD: the collect steps faked with a fixture, the rows they yield
# asserted. Two pages in, two inbox rows out, each with its source identity and its
# content, stamped with this pipeline's yields. The objects those rows become are the
# objects' own tests (objects/product/test.yaml), not this one.
testData:
  config:
    runId: run_fixture
  fake:
    pages:
      total: 2
      items:
        - { url: https://www.example.com/cards/aqsat, metadata: { title: AQSAT Credit Card, description: Shop now and pay later., openGraph: [{ property: "og:image", content: https://www.example.com/aqsat.png }] }, text: "Shop now...", markdown: "# AQSAT\n\nShop now and pay in instalments with no interest...", universalId: 3f1a9c2b7d4e, contentId: 9b8c7d6e5f4a }
        - { url: https://www.example.com/help/fees, metadata: { title: Fees and charges }, text: "Fees...", markdown: "# Fees\n\nAnnual fee, late payment fee, cash advance fee...", universalId: 5e6f7a8b9c0d, contentId: 1a2b3c4d5e6f }
  expect:
    rows: "return output.rows.length === 2"
    identity: "return output.rows.every(r => r.sourceUrl && r.sourceId)"
    content: "return output.rows.every(r => r.content.title && r.content.text.startsWith('# '))"
    image: "return output.rows[0].content.image === 'https://www.example.com/aqsat.png' && output.rows[1].content.image === undefined"
    yields: "return output.rows.every(r => r.yields.join(',') === 'need,product')"
